key_insight: Training 3D anomaly detectors with normal samples plus a small set of known defects (open-set supervised learning) substantially improves detection of previously unseen industrial defects; the paper also provides Open-Industry, a high-quality industrial 3D dataset to benchmark this setting.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between self-supervised 3D anomaly detection (which assumes no anomalous samples) and real manufacturing practice by enabling models trained with limited known anomalies to generalize to unknown defects at test time.
method: Introduce Open-Industry: a curated, high-precision industrial 3D point-cloud dataset containing normal parts and a small, representative set of labeled defects.
Formulate an open-set supervised training paradigm that uses normal samples plus a few known anomaly examples to learn discriminative 3D features.
Design generalisation-oriented objectives and 3D representation strategies (e.g., feature regularisation / contrastive-style separation) to improve detection of unseen defects at test time.
impact: Provides a practical, deployable approach for manufacturing anomaly detection when a limited number of defective examples are available and supplies a standardized dataset to accelerate research and benchmarking in open-set 3D anomaly detection.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data (normal + few known defects) → training strategy → test-time detection of unknown anomalies
Side-by-side point-cloud examples: normal vs known defect vs unknown defect (with anomaly masks/highlighted regions)
Performance chart: ROC/PR curves or bar plot comparing open-set supervised vs self-supervised baselines on the Open-Industry dataset
Feature-space visualization (e.g., t-SNE/UMAP): separation of normal, known anomalies, and clustering of unknown anomaly detections
paper_title: Open-Set Supervised 3D Anomaly Detection: An Industrial Dataset and a Generalisable Framework for Unknown Defects
paper_authors: Hanzhe Liang, Luocheng Zhang, Junyang Xia, HanLiang Zhou, Bingyang Guo
